narrative_note: On 2026-07-15 Stripe and Advent International submitted an unsolicited $60.50/share (~$53B) joint take-private proposal for PayPal; the board (advised by Goldman Sachs and Evercore) rejected it on 2026-07-20 as undervaluing the company, reportedly anchoring near $70/share, with some investors citing $110-115/share. Q2-2026 results (reported 2026-07-28) beat estimates and management raised FY2026 guidance (non-GAAP EPS ~$5.38, transaction margin dollars ~$15.6B, adjusted FCF >$6B, buybacks ~$6B). The stock rallied from ~$43 to ~$57 on these two events. This DCF values the business on standalone fundamentals; the rejected bid and board anchor are reference points only, not valuation inputs.

inputs.shares_outstanding_note: 882M is the Q2-2026 (2026-06-30) actual diluted-adjacent count, most current available; FY2025 year-end was 920M
inputs.net_debt_methodology: Total debt (13,400 = 2,505 ST + 10,895 LT) minus cash (8,306) minus short-term investments (2,950), as of 2026-06-30 10-Q. Long-term investments ($4,009M, largely illiquid/strategic) are excluded from the netting as a conservative choice. Net debt of $2,144M is modest relative to the ~$4.2B FY2025 owner-FCF base (well under 1x), so PayPal is NOT a material net-cash company by the interest-income-stripping rule of thumb.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: NOT stripped from FCF. PayPal carries net debt (not net cash) of $2.1B as of 2026-06-30, well below the 1x-FCF materiality threshold for stripping interest income. Interest income of $517M (FY2025) remains inside reported/owner FCF; it is not double-counted because net cash is not being added to enterprise value (net debt is subtracted instead).
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 cash flow statement (Stock-based compensation add-back, 'In millions') cross-referenced against 10-K FY2025 financing activities line 'Tax withholdings related to net share settlements of equity awards'. Both lines extracted directly from PYPL_10K_FY2025.txt; no combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation line is disclosed by PayPal, so the two cash-flow-statement lines are summed per the fallback methodology.
inputs.buyback_cash_source: 10-K FY2025 financing activities 'Purchases of treasury stock' = $6,052M; FY2026 guidance reiterates ~$6B pace ($1,500M Q1 + $1,552M Q2 actual per 10-Qs)
inputs.share_count_methodology: PayPal's ~$6B/yr buyback guidance far exceeds the ~$1.4-1.5B/yr SBC+equity-tax cash cost, so uncovered_dilution=0 and the share count DECLINES rather than grows. Modeled as: net_buyback_$[t] = buyback_cash[t] - sbc_incl_tax[t]; shares_repurchased[t] = net_buyback_$[t] / avg_price[t], where avg_price grows from the current $57.21 at a scenario-specific rate (base 12%/yr, bull 16%/yr, bear 6%/yr) to avoid a circular 'cheap stock buys back more shares to become even cheaper' feedback loop. The resulting base-case annualized share decline of 7.5%/yr is validated against realized history: shares fell 7.4%/yr over the trailing 3 years (2022-2025) and 8.1%/yr annualized over the trailing two quarters (FY2025 to Q2-2026).

sbc_noncash_memo.description: Memo: intrinsic value per share if SBC were treated as a non-cash expense (added back to FCF, all else equal) versus the actual owner-FCF treatment used in this model.
sbc_noncash_memo.interpretation: Roughly $23/share (~17% of the SBC-charged base-case IV) of headline value depends entirely on whether SBC is treated as a real cash cost. This model charges it as real (correct treatment).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: PayPal executes large buybacks (~$6B/yr, treasury stock now $33.1B), so equity growth (5yr CAGR +0.2%) massively understates economic growth and is NOT used as the growth driver, consistent with prior model. EPS 3yr CAGR (37.3%) is distorted upward by the FY2022 earnings trough (post-2021-bubble writedowns) and is not representative. Revenue CAGR (5yr 9.1%, 3yr 6.4%, most recent quarters ~5%) is used as the driver, decelerating toward FY2026 guidance-implied ~5%.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGR (3yr 6.0%, 5yr 6.2%) is actually ABOVE reported-FCF CAGR (3yr 2.9%, 5yr 2.2%) over the same periods -- the opposite of the usual pattern where SBC dilutes reported growth. This is because SBC+equity-tax cost fell in dollar terms from FY2021's elevated $2.4B (large RSU vesting/withholding year) to FY2025's $1.4B, so owner FCF's growth base benefited from a shrinking deduction even as reported FCF was volatile on working-capital timing (FY2023 reported FCF was depressed by loan-book/working-capital swings, FY2024 was inflated by the same). Reported FCF is NOT a clean growth series for PayPal; owner FCF, while still volatile, is the more consistent measure and is what this model's CAGRs and projections are built from.

horizon_rationale: PayPal is a mature $33B-revenue mega-cap already generating double-digit owner-FCF margins (12.6% actual FY2025). The base-case component build shows a gentle margin ramp (12.6% Y1 to 13.9% Y5, +1.3pp over 5 years) rather than a steep hypergrowth trajectory -- the year-5 margin is close to a plausible mature level, so a 5-year horizon is appropriate (unlike a still-scaling business where 10 years would be required).

base.terminal_value_used: gordon (computed at WACC, not the lower of gordon/cap -- per methodology TV_5 for entry price is always the Gordon value)

base_upside_gt_100pct_and_price_upper_ha.price_percentile: lower half (only 1 of 10 FY-end closes below current $57.21; range $39.47-$234.20, current sits well below the $136.84 midpoint)

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip rules fired. All implied multiples (P/E 31.2x, P/B 5.5x, EV/EBITDA 16.2x, P/S 3.4x) sit comfortably below their historical maxima even excluding the 2020-2021 bubble years, and well below the elevated 2018-2019 pre-maturity multiples. Base-case upside of 93.2% is below the 100% threshold (moderated during model-build from an initial 113% by raising WACC to 10.5% and using a less aggressive buyback-price-growth assumption for the share-count model -- see fix_applied). Even where upside exceeds 100% (weighted-case ~100%), the current price sits in the LOWER half of the 10-year range ($39.47-$234.20, midpoint $136.84), so the compound AND condition for the guardrail does not fire. The large absolute upside is explained by a genuine market dislocation: PayPal trades at $57.21 despite (a) a board-rejected $60.50/share cash buyout offer from Stripe/Advent, (b) the board's own ~$70/share fair-value anchor per public reporting, and (c) raised FY2026 guidance following a Q2-2026 beat. The DCF's $110.54 base IV is a standalone fundamental estimate, not calibrated to the takeover situation, and happens to sit meaningfully above even the board's stated anchor -- which is itself a useful cross-check that the DCF is not obviously too aggressive relative to an informed insider's view, though it should be read with appropriate humility given the size of the gap.
sanity_check.fix_applied: Initial base-case WACC of 10.0% and an 8%/yr buyback-driven share-count decline (assuming the reference price used to convert buyback dollars into retired shares grew at only 10%/yr, close to WACC) produced 113% base upside and a circular 'cheap stock buys back more shares, compounding value' dynamic that inflated IV by ~50% versus using today's share count. Fixed by: (1) raising base WACC to 10.5% (top of the 9.5-10.5% guided range, reflecting CEO-transition/competitive/execution risk), and (2) raising the buyback reference-price growth assumption to 12%/yr (base), 16%/yr (bull), 6%/yr (bear) so fewer shares are retired per dollar of buyback spend, which more conservatively decouples the DCF's own optimism from the pace of share-count shrinkage. This reduced base IV from $121.88 to $110.54 and base upside from 113.0% to 93.2%, still validated against realized 3-year (-7.4%/yr) and trailing-2-quarter (-8.1%/yr annualized) actual share-count decline rates.
